The four rows of data are respectively: when X=0, Y=0, f(X,Y)=0; when X=0, Y=1, f(X,Y)=0; when X=1, Y=0, f(X,Y)=1; when X=1, Y=1, f(X,Y)=1. method.method_draft: First describe the image as a three-column truth table with columns X, Y, and f(X,Y). Transcribe each row from the image and compare the f(X,Y) values with the X values row by row. Because every output equals the corresponding X value regardless of Y, conclude that the Boolean function represented is f(X,Y)=X.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct truth-table pattern matching is the natural and essentially unique route: compare the output column against each input column and identify the identical column.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the table headers X, Y, and f(X,Y), then transcribe the four rows: for (X,Y) = (0,0) output 0; (0,1) output 0; (1,0) output 1; (1,1) output 1. Observe that the output column is 0,0,1,1, exactly the same as the X column, while it does not match the Y column.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to know that the task is to name the Boolean function represented by the truth table.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the Boolean-function rule that if f has the same value as an input variable for every row of the truth table, then f equals that variable. Since f(X,Y) matches X for all input combinations, the represented function is X.
